rules.sourceConstruct: WebDriver.FindElement(By.Id("literal")) inline on an action target
rules.targetConstruct: Page.Locator("#literal") (TargetKind.RawExpression)
rules.emitterImplementation: DotNetLocatorRenderer / RenderTargetExpression; action emitter (e.g. RenderClick, RenderSendKeys) in PlaywrightDotNetRenderer.cs
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: FindElement (single) and FindElements (collection) are matched by the same regex (FindElements?), i.e. cardinality is conflated in the default resolver. Without adapter-config this rule is NOT applied to inline action targets (evidence: p01 run -> 3 unmapped By.Id targets); it IS applied to the same expression inside a local declaration (p01 line 15 `var result = ...` -> `Page.Locator("#result")`). Path-dependence confirmed.
rules.testsCoveringRule: corpus p01 (mapped in lab generated config), SnapshotTests
rules.knownMissingCases: dynamic Id/attributes, non-literal selectors, Name/ClassName/PartialLinkText, custom locator helpers
rules.note: CONFIRMED path inconsistency: inline vs declaration resolution differ in the unconfigured default path.

rules.targetConstruct: Page.Locator("literal")

rules.knownSemanticDifferences: none for literal CSS given an identical selector; collection vs single conflated (FindElements?)
rules.knownMissingCases: dynamic css, nested/relative selectors

rules.fallbackBehavior: dynamic xpath -> UnsupportedAction "add MethodMapping"; unresolved -> TODO
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: Playwright XPath scoping is relative to locator root; Selenium XPath `//` is document-wide. Same-string xpath can behave differently inside composed locators. Kept verbatim, so signal preserved but composition risk exists.
rules.knownMissingCases: xpath containing escaped quotes/interpolation inside xpath function, axis expressions with predicates referencing page state

rules.targetConstruct: Page.Locator($"#...{expr}..."))

rules.sourceConstruct: local locator variable and By alias: var x = WebDriver.FindElement(By.Id(...)); later x.Click() / By.Alias
rules.sourceSymbolsRecognized: none (syntax rewriter SeleniumByAliasNormalizer + localVariableMappings tracking in adapter)
rules.targetConstruct: Page.Locator(...) local + reuse via mapping; local.ElementAt(i)/local[i] -> Locator.Nth(i) (ResolveLocalElementAt/IndexedAccess :1020-1065)
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: Selenium IWebElement is a *stored snapshot*; Playwright ILocator is *lazy and evaluated per action*. Semantics differ under DOM mutation / stale element. Cardinality of FindElements stored list not modelled (only ElementAt[i] index handled).
rules.knownMissingCases: stale element patterns, re-query semantics, element stored then page reloaded

rules.recognizerImplementation: DefaultProjectAdapter + WebDriverFindElementRecognizer regexes treat FindElement and FindElements identically
rules.targetConstruct: same Page.Locator(...) as single; Nth(i) only when indexed; Count via TableCountAssertion paths
rules.fallbackBehavior: indexed access -> Nth; bare multi-match locator kept (strict-mode violation at runtime if used as single)
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: Selenium FindElements returns count at call time; Playwright locator re-evaluates. `Count` after mutation, ordering stability, and implicit-wait interplay differ. Multi-match locator used for a single action throws strict-mode violation in Playwright where Selenium returned the first — a semantic trap.
rules.knownMissingCases: foreach over FindElements where body asserts per element; filters; last/first match policy is config Match only
rules.note: Cardinality conflation is a CONFIRMED risk: FindElement vs FindElements not distinguished by recognizers.

Usually a strict improvement, but changes timing and can hang rather than fail fast; also Click via Actions (move+click) not equivalent.

rules.sourceSymbolsRecognized: SendKeysInvocationRecognizer (syntax, configured InputMethods incl. default SendKeys/InputText); semantic path when Selenium type
rules.targetConstruct: await <locator>.FillAsync(value)
rules.fallbackBehavior: unresolved target -> TODO; missing value -> TODO
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: CONFIRMED semantic difference: Selenium SendKeys *types key-by-key* (fires keydown/keypress/keyup, increments existing value, can fail on readonly?) while Playwright Fill *sets value directly* (one input event, overwrites). Sending keys with modifiers, tab order, autocomplete, per-key delays, and apps that listen to key events differ. The migrator maps SendKeys -> FillAsync without distinction. Keys.* constants -> PressAsync (keyboard semantics preserved better).
rules.testsCoveringRule: corpus p01, p02, p13; keyboard Keys.Enter cases
rules.knownMissingCases: SendKeys with Keys combination (e.g. Keys.Control+"a"), clear+type composition, IME, input with keydown handlers

rules.targetConstruct: await <locator>.PressAsync("Enter"|"Tab"|...)
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: Key name mapping is ad hoc; Selenium Keys.Enter is a terminal key while Playwright PressAsync("Enter") is generally equivalent; some keys (Keys.Null, unicode) unmapped
rules.knownMissingCases: Selenium special-key universe not fully enumerated

rules.targetConstruct: WaitForAction(ActionabilityElided) -> elided as comment: "source wait elided ... Playwright actions and web-first assertions auto-wait for actionability."
rules.emitterImplementation: DotNetAssertionAndWaitRenderer.RenderWaitFor ActionabilityElided branch (comment only, no emitted statement)
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: Elision assumes Playwright auto-wait covers the *specific* intent (visible vs enabled vs clickable are different states). Presence (attached) is not actionability-identical. If the element is present-but-hidden more or fewer waits happen. Not a no-op semantically.
rules.knownMissingCases: WaitPresence where element stays hidden (catch explicit visible check)
rules.note: Elision is a deliberate semantic-loss decision made textually, not by per-state analysis.

rules.sourceConstruct: product-state waits inferred from method NAME: WaitForLoaded/WaitTableLoaded/Wait for Loader/Spinner/Modal/Toast/Table/Grid/Results ...
rules.sourceSymbolsRecognized: WaitInvocationRecognizer.IsProductStateWait + InferProductStateKind using verb/widget heuristics (ClosingStateVerbs/OpeningStateVerbs, widget buckets)
rules.targetConstruct: WaitForAction(ProductStateVisible|Hidden|Loaded) -> Expect(locator).ToBeVisibleAsync/ToBeHiddenAsync/WaitForAsync or ReviewRequired
rules.knownSemanticDifferences: CONFIRMED unsafe-by-construction heuristic: the *target locator of a product-state wait is the wait receiver*, which is frequently NOT the element whose state matters (e.g. page.WaitForLoaderModal() waits the modal container, not the hidden loader). Direction (Visible vs Hidden) guessed from names like Wait{Toast}->Visible even though toasts usually *disappear*. Method-name-only semantics cannot prove the intended product state.

rules.sourceConstruct: Fluent text assertion: x.Text().Get().Should().Be("..") / NotBe / Contain / BeEmpty / NotBeEmpty (Selone-style)

Also full-text vs trimmed-content differences.
